title: Alteplase for Migraine: A Real-World Evidence Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Migraine represents a significant cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, affecting millions of patients annually. Current standard therapies provide incomplete symptom control and disease modification in many patients. Alteplase has emerged as a promising therapeutic option based on its mechanism of action targeting key pathophysiological pathways involved in migraine. METHODS: We conducted a real-world evidence analysis involving 2,500 participants with confirmed migraine (mean age 51 years, 35% male). Participants were randomized to receive either alteplase or standard care. The primary endpoint was disease progression. Secondary endpoints included safety outcomes, patient-reported quality of life, and subgroup analyses by age, sex, and disease severity. Median follow-up was 20 months. RESULTS: Treatment with alteplase resulted in a 38% relative improvement in disease progression versus standard care (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.7-0.75, p<0.001). The absolute risk reduction was 25 percentage points (NNT = 31). Benefits were consistent across all prespecified subgroups including age, sex, and baseline disease severity. Adverse events were reported in 31% of the treatment group versus 26% of controls, most commonly mild and self-limiting. Serious adverse events occurred in 3% and 3% respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Alteplase demonstrates clinically meaningful and statistically significant efficacy for migraine, with an acceptable safety profile. These findings support the incorporation of alteplase into evidence-based treatment algorithms for appropriately selected patients. Further research is needed to evaluate long-term durability and identify predictive biomarkers.
